newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened against the dollar on Tuesday in thin trading, responding to the rise of the U.S. currency abroad, dealers said.
"There was almost no trading today since many banks and investors were suffering from communications problems because of the phone strike," said Gideon Sadeh at Bank Leumi.

A week-long strike over government plans to privatise more of Bezeq Israel Telcom has curtailed telephone repair and operator information services. By Tuesday many businesses were suffering communications problems.
"Volume was very low and the only reason for the shekel's decline against the dollar was the rise of the U.S. currency abroad," Sadeh said.
The dollar strode on Tuesday to a new 71-month high against the mark in Europe.
"Just before the setting of the representative rate activity rose and the shekel started rising for no evident reason," he added.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5300 shekels compared with 3.5240 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7952 against 3.7981 on Monday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded at 3.0431 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.0424 on Monday, and against the mark at 1.9473 shekels compared with 1.9651 on Monday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5285 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233 DMG
